reason:
Reproduced both sequences at 1440. Five presses of "Move a day earlier" moves "Send the invitations" 23 -> 18 and sets --push:54px on its .b-copy only: the count "18" paints at y608-632 and its tick at y612, while its own title does not begin until y660. The band the count occupies is the same band as the row above's date line, "Sat 1 Aug" at y602-617. Reading across the gutter — the only reading an instrument this literal invites — pairs 18 with 1 Aug, which is 16 days out, not 18. The Add case is worse than the finding states: five presses of "Add a moment" produce pushes of 102/196/272/236/200/164px, and the gutter then reads 1, 2, 9, 16, 23 against copy blocks dated Fri 17 Jul, Fri 17 Jul, Fri 17 Jul, Sat 18 Jul, Sat 25 Jul. Every pairing is false by two or three rows: "9" sits level with a moment that is 1 day away, "23" level with one that is 9 days away. The measured delta between .b-away top and its own .b-copy top reaches 270px. This is the product's central claim — position is the quantity — being contradicted by the numeric column that states the quantity.

Not already handled. The only crowded treatment is b.css:337, .b-item[data-crowded="true"] .b-copy { box-shadow: 0 0 0 12px var(--back) }, which knocks a card out behind the pushed words. It separates the block but associates it with nothing, and it makes the reading worse rather than better: the card boundary begins below the count, so the count is drawn outside its own moment's card and inside the space of the one above. Nothing joins a mark to its words. The finding is right that data-stack lead/follow already solves exactly this problem for two moments on the same day and simply stops at one day apart.

Not restated by the gates. collisions() in interaction-check.mjs (lines 159-171) maps only .b-copy rects and is commented "The tick and the count sit on the true pixel; the words are what must not overlap" — the whole class is outside what it measures. "measure is strictly proportional" reads .b-item offsetTop, and "every count matches its own date" compares textContent; neither looks at where the count is painted.

No constraint is touched: the fix is ink tint, no hue, no weight, no structural change.

On the crux the brief names — should the count follow the pushed words or stay with the tick — the finding's answer is right. The tick is the position and carries the truth on its own; the count is the position said in words, and a number is only meaningful paired with the moment it names. A count that stays on the true pixel while its words leave is not more truthful, it is a true number attached to the wrong row. The system already concedes the principle: for a same-day stack it hides the follow row's count entirely and lets one count cover words that sit well below it, because grouping, not pixel-exactness, is what makes the count readable.

The finding is loose in two places, neither fatal: the stepper gap is 52px title-top to count-top (48px from the tick), not 76px, and the Add gap is 270px, not 266px.

What must not be taken as written is the proposed fix, which fails mechanically in three ways — see sharpenedFix.
sharpenedFix:
Right diagnosis, wrong mechanics — all three halves of the proposed fix are inoperative as written; verified by measurement.

1. The leader is invisible at phone and misplaced at desk. .b-rail is 1px of var(--fore-16). Measured, .b-item left minus .b-rail left is 20px at 390 and 24px at 1440 (responsive overrides move both). So an ::after at left:-20px with background var(--fore-16) lands exactly on the rail, same width, same colour, at 390 — a pixel-identical no-op — and at 1440 lands 4px right of the rail on the tick's right edge rather than its centre. Draw the leader as an overprint of the rail, not a second line beside it: position it off the tick (left: calc(-23px + 3px) at the desk value, or better, derive it from the same custom property the rail and tick already share) and give it a density the rail does not have, var(--fore-46), so it reads as a brighter stretch of rail claimed by one moment. Cap the drawn height and fade the tail where --lead exceeds about 120px, or the Add case paints a 270px bar.

2. --push does not reach .b-away. place() sets it with copy.style.setProperty("--push", ...) on the .b-copy element; .b-away is its sibling, so it inherits nothing and "margin-top: var(--push, 0px)" resolves to the 0px fallback every time. Set --push on the .b-item in place() instead (and keep .b-copy reading it by inheritance), then move the count with transform: translateY(var(--push, 0px)) rather than margin-top — .b-away is position:absolute with top:2px, and a transform avoids the abspos margin resolution entirely and animates with the existing --t-slow transition instead of jumping.

3. The proposed gate assertion misses the defect. Measured after twenty presses of "Move a day earlier", the moment has travelled 23 -> 3, clear of everything, and every push is 0px: the twenty-press state is clean at both 390 and 1440. The collision window is transient — it opens around press five and closes again. Assert after EVERY press, not only the last, and after each of the five adds: for every .b-item that is not data-stack="follow", abs(.b-away top - its own .b-copy top) < 4px, at 390 and 1440. Add one assertion the current gate has no equivalent of — that no .b-away rect vertically overlaps any other item's .b-date rect — since that is the specific false reading, and it is the one thing collisions() structurally cannot see.
